dedupe_keys.name: waste atlas global map of waste management data

description: Waste Atlas is a crowdsourced, non-commercial interactive map of solid waste management around the world. Country layers give municipal solid waste generation, per capita generation, collection coverage, recycling rate and share of unsound disposal; city layers cover 1,799 cities; facility layers locate 1,626 sanitary landfills, 93 large dumpsites, 130 mechanical-biological treatment units, 78 biological treatment plants and 716 waste-to-energy plants, with capacity, area, waste in place and population served where known. The provider is D-Waste, whose founder presented the atlas as a planning tool; its annual reports profiled the world's 50 biggest dumpsites in 2014. Coverage is global, compiled mostly around 2012–2014 from national reports, literature and user submissions. Data are viewed through the web map and charts free of charge, under the site's legal notice for non-commercial use; no bulk download or open licence is offered. Caveats: facility coverage is uneven and self-reported, values come from different years and definitions, and the atlas appears not to have been updated since its 2014 report. Simulation uses: a starting inventory of large disposal and treatment facilities for hazard exposure of waste infrastructure (for example coastal dumpsites) and regional capacity planning. Related records: the What a Waste global database (data-what-a-waste-global-database) is the maintained source for country and city waste statistics.
